crs_note: British National Grid. Every raster and vector in the pipeline is held in this CRS; OSM arrives in WGS84 degrees and is reprojected by step 01.
crs_max_transform_accuracy_note: Step 01 refuses to reproject OSM unless PROJ's best available WGS84 -> CRS operation is at least this accurate: the OSTN15 grid (1 m class), not the 2 m Helmert fallback that silently applies when the grid file is missing and shifts the model ~1.8 m off the LIDAR.
origin_note: South-west corner of the tile grid, in CRS units. Whitby town centre is NZ893109 (E 489300, N 510900); the grid takes in the harbour, West Cliff, the East Cliff / abbey headland (E 490300, N 511200) and a row of sea to the north.
grid_res_note: Samples per tile edge. 513 = 512 + 1 so adjacent tiles share an identical edge row and there is no seam.
bbox_note: S,W,N,E -- Overpass order. Generous on purpose; features outside the tile grid are counted and dropped by steps 06/07/10.
vertical_datum_note: Ordnance Datum Newlyn -- the datum of the EA LIDAR. Every elevation the pipeline emits, including water_level, is metres above this.
water_level_note: MEASURED from the EA DTM tiles fetched by step 02 on 2026-09-07. The composite carries the surveyed water surface over the open sea and the harbour as one broad peak: mode -2.25 m ODN, 1.3M locally-flat cells between -2.6 and -2.0, then a thin tail up to -0.9 that is exposed low-tide sand. The survey was flown near low water; Whitby's tidal range is ~5 m. Every tile has data -- there is no no-DTM sea here. Note the first-return DSM does NOT share this coverage: it has flight-strip gaps over 187 ha of land, which is why step 04 samples ground and height independently.

height_calib.note: mode auto: step 07 regresses height = intercept + m_per_level * building:levels from this site's own buildings that carry both a levels tag and a trustworthy LIDAR p50, records the fit in massing_manifest.json, and uses it. EXPECT THE FALLBACK HERE: the 2026-09-07 Overpass extract holds 3,330 buildings and only 2 carry building:levels, so no fit is possible and the manifest will say source=fallback. It barely matters -- LIDAR coverage is 100%, so nearly every height is lidar_p50 and the osm_levels rung almost never fires. The fallback is Margate's line, not a measurement of Whitby.

coast.water_tolerance_note: MEASURED: the sea-surface peak spans -2.6..-2.0 m around water_level -2.3, so +/-0.4 takes the whole peak; the tail above -1.9 is left as foreshore sand. Anything below the water level is water regardless.
coast.note: foreshore_max_odn is PROVISIONAL: the DTM shows the sea at -2.3 m, so sand lies between that and roughly mean high water springs (~2.5 m ODN here); check it does not paint the harbour quays. rock_slope_deg was checked against the real DTM: the shale cliffs measure a 53 degree median face (28 m wide for a 31 m drop), so a 25-45 ramp reads them as rock. water_tolerance_m: cells within this of water_level and flat are classified water -- the DTM's sea surface is a plane, not ground. missing_tiles_are_water: all 30 tiles have data here, so it is irrelevant; leave false unless a site has no-DTM tiles that are known to be open sea.

landmarks._note: None yet, deliberately. Hand overrides are for buildings the LIDAR p50 estimator provably gets wrong -- add them after reading qa_height_outliers.json from the first run, not before. Candidates: Whitby Abbey (roofless ruin -- p50 samples the floor between the walls) and St Mary's church tower.
